identity.title: exoALMA XXII: A Two-dimensional Atlas of Deviations from Keplerian Disks

paper_type_evidence.quote: Using the the CO ($J$=3–2) data from the exoALMA Large Program encompassing 15 disks, we constructed two-dimensional (2D) maps of centroid velocity, line width, and peak intensity

targets.name: 15 exoALMA disks (AA Tau, CQ Tau, DM Tau, HD 135344B, HD 143006, HD 34282, J1604, J1615, J1842, J1852, LkCa 15, MWC 758, PDS 66, SY Cha, V4046 Sgr)

question.value: How do the 2D maps of centroid velocity, line width and peak intensity in CO deviate from smooth Keplerian disks across the 15 exoALMA disks?

evidence.quote: We provide an overview of how the observed velocity and intensity distributions deviate from those expected for a Keplerian rotating disk
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2021.1.01123.L.
the data from $^{12}$CO ($J$=3–2), which have high S/N, are mainly used
The images in $^{13}$CO ($J$=3–2) and CS ($J$=7–6) are included in the Appendix
The images in $^{13}$CO ($J$=3–2) and CS ($J$=7–6) are included in the Appendix
images with beam sizes of $0.15\ensuremath{''}$ or $0.30\ensuremath{''}$ and velocity resolutions of 28 m s$^{-1}$, 100 m s$^{-1}$, or 200 m s$^{-1}$ are utilized

what.value: Emission-surface heights, mean z/r of 0.28 (12CO) and 0.16 (13CO)

evidence.quote: obtaining $\langle$$z/r$$\rangle$=0.28 and 0.16 for $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO, respectively

what.value: Disk gas masses from rotation curves with self-gravity

evidence.quote: disk masses estimated by (cite: exoALMA_rotation_curve) for 10 exoALMA sources from the rotation curves with gas self-gravity taken into account
While a synthesized beam size of $0.15\ensuremath{''}$ and a velocity resolution of 100 m s$^{-1}$ are used as the baseline
The data were calibrated and imaged as detailed in (cite: exoALMA_calimg).

what.value: Moment maps, residuals and DISCMINER modelling, including kernels and best-fit parameters

evidence.quote: following the analysis method presented in (cite: exoALMA_discminer)

unstated_but_needed: Best-fit DISCMINER parameters and kernel for each source (only in Izquierdo et al. 2025)
Masking radii used in DISCMINER fitting
Residual-map colour scales and detection criteria for substructures

method.value: Line-profile fitting with the best-performing kernel per source and species (Gaussian, bell, double-bell, double-Gaussian)

evidence.quote: single-component (Gaussian, bell) and double-component (double-bell, double-Gaussian) fitting kernels were all tested and the one that best reproduced the observed spectral profiles was selected

analysis_steps.goal: Fit smooth Keplerian model and make residuals

method.value: Parametric Keplerian disk model fitted to channel maps and subtracted from the observed maps

evidence.quote: Residual maps were created by subtracting the model disk obtained from spectral fitting using DISCMINER

method.value: Visual classification of velocity residuals into spiral, arc/ring and other, then comparison with line-width and peak-intensity residuals

evidence.quote: we roughly classify the sources into three categories according to the spatial distribution of the residuals: (1) spiral, (2) arc- or ring-like, and (3) other types
We also do not discuss the inner region within approximately $0.3\ensuremath{''}$

validation.value: 13CO maps used to support the reliability of features seen in 12CO

evidence.quote: can therefore be used to support the reliability of the features seen in $^{12}$CO

used_for.value: Moment-map extraction by line-profile fitting and Keplerian disk model fitting

evidence.quote: The extraction of moment maps and the fitting of a smooth Keplerian disk to the data from the observations were performed using DISCMINER
obtaining $\langle$$z/r$$\rangle$=0.28 and 0.16 for $^{12}$CO and $^{13}$CO, respectively

findings_qualitative.value: All 15 targets show large-scale deviations from smooth Keplerian disks.

evidence.quote: We find that all targets exhibit large-scale deviations from smooth Keplerian disks

findings_qualitative.value: Spiral arms are detected or suggested in CQ Tau, MWC 758, HD 135344B, HD 34282 and SY Cha.

evidence.quote: Non-axisymmetric spiral-arm features are detected or suggested in five disks (CQ Tau, MWC 758, HD 135344B, HD 34282, and SY Cha)

claims.hypothesis: Do large protoplanetary disks have kinematic deviations from Keplerian rotation?
claims.experiment: 2D residual maps of velocity, line width and peak intensity from DISCMINER for 15 disks
claims.finding: Kinematic substructures are ubiquitous in large disks

evidence.quote: This 2D atlas suggests that kinematic substructures are ubiquitous in large ($\gtrsim 100$ au) protoplanetary disks

claims.hypothesis: Are spirals preferentially found in Herbig Ae/Fe disks?
claims.result: Spirals in five disks, mostly Herbig
claims.finding: Spirals preferentially in Herbig Ae/Fe systems

evidence.quote: and are preferentially found in Herbig Ae/Fe systems

claims.experiment: Comparison of residuals across the three observables
claims.result: J1852, PDS 66 and V4046 Sgr lack prominent substructures

evidence.quote: J1852, PDS 66, and V4046 Sgr appear dynamically more quiescent than the other disks

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Quadrupole residuals may result from a mismatch in emitting-surface height rather than dynamics.

evidence.quote: non-Keplerian features symmetric with respect to the disk minor axis may originate from a mismatch between the actual emitting surface of the disk and the fitted smooth disk model

limitations_admitted.value: Sample is biased toward large disks and not representative.

evidence.quote: the sample is biased toward large ($>$1$\ensuremath{''}$) disks and is not representative of the full disk population

referee_caveats_inferred: Classification is visual and qualitative, with no quantitative detection thresholds
Residuals depend on the smooth-model fit and can reflect surface-height or geometry mismatch
Sample of 15 limits the Herbig vs T Tauri comparison

data_public_as_stated.value: Line cubes and residual images are available on the exoALMA website

evidence.quote: The data underlying this study, including the generated line cubes and residual images, are made available at: https://www.exoalma.com/home
https://github.com/andizq/discminer

missing_for_reproduction: Fit parameters from the DISCMINER paper
Calibration and imaging details from the companion papers
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Large Program of 15 disks; hundreds of GB for raw data, with released cubes smaller
reproducibility.score_reason: The paper is a qualitative atlas that relies on companion papers for the processing, but it uses public products and a public code.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Results are qualitative morphological classifications and depend on companion-paper recipes.
